Introduction
Th e endocrine system is more of a complex functional system
than an anatomical system. Endocrine glands that make up the 
endocrine system are not attached anatomically, but scattered
all through the body. All the same, these glands make up a
system in a functional sense, since their regulatory activities are 
often interdependent and must be closely coordinated.

hormones (chemical messengers) into the blood, and nu-
merous interactions occur between the various glands (see
